instruction: Add the webpage I'm currently viewing to the bookmarks bar.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully saved the current webpage as PDF to Desktop with no margins. Used Ctrl+P to open print dialog, expanded More Settings, changed margins to None, navigated to Desktop in file save dialog, and saved with default filename. Then verified file existence via Files app.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use Ctrl+P for print dialog, navigate print settings (margins, layout), use file save dialog to choose destination folder, interact with Chrome browser, search and open desktop applications
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different Chrome interaction pattern (bookmarking) using the same webpage setup. The model demonstrated strong Chrome navigation ability, so bookmarking is a related browser task at similar difficulty.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding the current page to the bookmarks bar. Evaluator uses official bookmarks getter to retrieve all bookmarks and is_expected_bookmarks metric to verify the target URL appears in the bookmarks bar.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'get_bookmarks' correctly reads Chrome's Bookmarks file and returns the roots dictionary containing bookmark_bar data needed by the metric.
Metric 'is_expected_bookmarks' correctly handles the 'bookmark_bar_websites_urls' rule type, extracting URLs from bookmark_bar children and comparing against expected URLs.
Expected parameter handling is correct: get_rule returns the rules dict directly, and the metric accesses rule['type'] and rule['urls'] without incorrect nesting.
The expected URL matches the URL opened in the config, correctly verifying the instruction requirement.

Minor concern: metric uses set equality (==) which requires bookmark bar to contain ONLY the expected URLs. Pre-existing bookmarks would cause false negatives, though the OSWorld environment is typically clean.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using set.issubset() instead of set equality to allow pre-existing bookmarks in the bookmark bar, making the check more robust: 'set(rule["urls"]).issubset(set(bookmark_bar_websites_urls))'
